Management Plan
2026
Directorate-General Health and Food Safety
(SANTE)
1

PART 1. Introduction
The Directorate-General for Health and Food
Safety (DG SANTE) strives to protect human,
animal and plant health, to promote high
levels of food and feed safety, as well as of
animal welfare, and to enable the health and
food sectors to achieve their full economic
potential. The One Health approach, linking
the health of humans, animals, plants, and
the wider environment underpins DG SANTE
action to prevent, prepare for and respond to threats at EU level and beyond. Our mission
supports the Commission’s priorities in two of the EU’s most important economic sectors –
health and food. Strategic planning and programming is the cornerstone of the Commission’s
performance management framework. The Commission’s strategic plan for 2025-2029
translates the political priorities set in the Political Guidelines of President von der Leyen into
general objectives. This process ensures institutional coherence, enhances accountability, and
aligns the actions of all Commission services with the strategic vision of the mandate.
Within this framework, each Commission service has developed a strategic outlook for
2025-2029 in its 2025 Management Plan. This outlook defines a set of multiannual objectives
and indicators to measure progress towards their achievement. These will be used for planning
and reporting on performance throughout the period.
The 2026 Management Plan sets out what DG SANTE intends to deliver this year to
contribute to these multiannual objectives (part 2). It also describes how DG SANTE will
contribute to the common objective of building a modern and sustainable public administration
(part 3). The main outputs with their indicators and targets are presented in Annexes 1 and 2.
The chart below illustrates the performance framework for DG SANTE.
3

DG SANTE’s specific objectives and selected key performance indicators 2025-2029
DG SANTE’s target for the estimated risk at payment remains to be below 2% of relevant
expenditure. The same target is applied to the estimated risk at closure because no corrections
are expected to be implemented.
4

PART 2. Delivering on the Commission’s
priorities in 2026
General Objective 1: A new plan for Europe’s
sustainable prosperity and competitiveness
DG SANTE works to ensure that the key legislation in health is implemented, given its critical
importance to the well-being of EU citizens. Implementing the rules ensure that the EU remains
an attractive and competitive market for innovative products and services and that it
contributes to the EU’s global leadership in health and food and feed safety.
Specific objective 1.1: Improve the competitiveness of the
European health sector through innovation
In 2026, DG SANTE will work with the European Parliament and the Council during the
negotiations on the proposal for a European Biotech Act. A key initiative of the Commission,
the Biotech Act has enormous potential to foster competitiveness and innovation in the EU
across sectors and will contribute to the Commission’s simplification agenda.
DG SANTE will prepare to implement the reform of the pharmaceutical legislation, which
will modernise, simplify and facilitate the rules and improve the structure of the European
Medicines Agency, supporting both innovation and competitiveness in the sector. This will
require a number of delegated and implementing acts.
DG SANTE will work with the co-legislators in the negotiations on the targeted revision of
the Regulations on medical devices and in vitro diagnostic medical devices. The
proposal aims to simplify the current rules, reduce burdens, foster innovation and promote
competitiveness to benefit patients. It will ensure the availability of safe and innovative devices
and safeguard a high level of patient safety, public health and healthcare. DG SANTE will
organise a high-level conference on medical devices on 16 March 2026 to present the progress
made, taking into consideration the outcomes of the targeted evaluation and the Commission
proposal.
Another strand of work will focus on making the European
Health Data Space (EHDS) a reality, including through the
adoption of implementing acts. The EHDS will allow health data to
be accessed and shared to boost innovation in healthcare, which
will in turn support competitiveness. The EHDS will be critical for
accelerating innovation in Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare.
An implementation dialogue on the European Health Data Space
will take place in the first half of the year.
5

Similarly, implementing the Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Regulation will help
make the health technology sector in Europe more attractive and competitive and increase
access to innovative products. Under the Regulation, as of 12 January 2025, all new cancer
medicines and advanced therapy medicinal products that seek central marketing authorisation
are subject to a joint clinical assessment, and can be selected by the Coordination Group. In
2026, around 10 joint clinical assessment reports are expected to be published, serving as a
basis for Member States to make their reimbursement decisions on these new health
technologies.
In addition, the 2026 Annual Progress Report on Simplification, Implementation and
Enforcement will be prepared for submission by the Commissioner to the respective
Parliamentary committees and Council configurations.
Specific objective 1.2: Resilient and effective health systems
providing accessible and equitable healthcare
In 2026, DG SANTE will work with the European Parliament and the Council in the negotiations
on the Critical Medicines Act and will prepare to implement it. This includes setting up the
coordination group, exploring strategic partnerships and issuing guidance on public procurement
and contingency stocks (1). The Act aims to address severe shortages and reduce dependencies
for critical medicines, as well as improve access to and availability of other medicines of
common interest.
On Substances of Human Origin (SoHO), work will focus on implementing the new EU rules
ahead of their full application in 2027. This requires adopting delegated and implementing acts,
developing an IT platform and for guidance to be set out through the new SoHO Coordination
Board. The new framework will facilitate the uptake of biotech and innovation and ensure the
supply of safe and qualitative substances of human origin. The framework will ensure that
citizens are better protected when donating and receiving substances such as blood, tissues,
cells, breast milk or microbiota and derived medicines such as plasma derivatives; and that
they can count on access to such essential substances.
In 2026, DG SANTE will start preparing for the implementation report on the Cross-border
Healthcare Directive. The Directive provides EU citizens with the right to access healthcare in
any EU country and to be reimbursed for care abroad. It also encourages the development of
European Reference Networks (ERNs), bringing together European hospital centres of
expertise and reference to tackle rare, low prevalence and complex diseases and conditions
requiring highly specialised healthcare. DG SANTE will promote better awareness of the work of
the European Reference Networks. This work will build on the dedicated workshops organised in
12 EU countries over 2024 and 2025.
(1) Subject to the outcome of interinstitutional negotiations.
6

The EU4Health Programme will financially support EU
priorities in health, supporting the implementation of the
existing health rules, steering innovation uptake in
healthcare and contributing to building a strong European
Health Union (2). In early 2026, under the 2025 work
programme of the EU4Health Programme, the European
flagship initiative leveraging AI and health data for cardiovascular health and
related non-communicable diseases will be launched through several projects as a matter
of priority, with a view to piloting the use of data-driven AI solutions.
DG SANTE will provide country-specific information and analysis on health and health systems
as part of the European Semester. Work will also include assessing Member States’ progress
on European Semester Country-Specific Recommendations on health. DG SANTE will
monitor the health-related milestones and targets of the 27 national recovery and
resilience plans under the Recovery and Resilience Facility ahead of the Facility’s closure
in 2026. In addition, new and updated Country-Specific Recommendations on health in the
2026 European Semester should guide Member States in prioritising reforms and investments
under the proposed National and Regional Partnership Plans. By the end of 2026, DG SANTE
will issue a new Health at a Glance: Europe report as part of the State of health in the EU
project.
The Expert Group on Health Systems Performance Assessment is expected to issue a
report on healthcare staffing levels in 2026. A number of EU4Health projects will focus on
health workforce, including the Joint Action on Health Workforce planning, training projects, a
project on nurse shortages with the World Health Organization, and the BEWELL health skills
multi-stakeholder partnership (Erasmus+).
The Commission will engage with a wide range of health stakeholders through the Health
Policy Platform. The Platform serves as a mechanism for stakeholder involvement and
consultation for over 7000 organisations, supporting DG SANTE and stakeholders with webinars
(60 webinars on average per year) and online networks (44 specific networks).
General objective 2: A new era for European
defence and security
Through stronger and coordinated prevention, preparedness and response actions, the Union
will be able to react to future health crises in a timely and efficient manner and help
strengthen global health security.
(2) While listed under specific objective 1.2, the EU4Health Programme also contributes to
specific objectives 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 and 3.1.
7

Specific objective 2.1: Strengthened health security, through
preparedness for, prevention of and response to serious
cross-border threats to health
DG SANTE will work on implementing the regulation on serious cross-border threats to
health, which provides the EU with stronger rules on how to prevent, prepare for and respond
to major health threats. The rules form part of the EU’s health security infrastructure and will
help keep countries prepared in a rapidly changing world. DG SANTE will enhance threat
detection and surveillance systems by establishing EU Reference Laboratories and further
strengthen civil-military collaboration in health security. DG SANTE will conduct a simulation
exercise to ensure that the Union Prevention, Preparedness and Response Plan for Health
Crises, adopted on 28 November 2025, effectively meets its intended goals. In 2026, DG SANTE
will report to the European Parliament and Council on the state of preparedness. In 2026, DG
SANTE will also publish its evaluation of the regulation on serious cross-border threats to
health.
DG SANTE will also manage surveillance, alerts and response to health threats in coordination
with the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. In 2026, DG SANTE will
publish its evaluation of the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control.
DG SANTE, together with DG INTPA, will coordinate and help implement the EU Global Health
Strategy (3) and the Global Health Resilience initiative that will be launched in 2026. Both
aim to improve global health security and deliver better health for all in a changing world.
Specific objective 2.2: Implementing a One Health approach
DG SANTE will actively promote the One
Health approach, recognising the
interdependence between people, animals,
plants and their shared environment. This
includes stronger coordination internally in
the Commission, with EU agencies and with
Member States and stakeholders. It will
also be reflected in the work on pandemic
prevention, preparedness, and response,
improving the global health security
architecture, investigating food-borne outbreaks, and fighting antimicrobial resistance.
SANTE’s work on animal welfare will help reduce antimicrobial resistance, as better conditions
for animals reduce the need for medications. DG SANTE works with Member States to prevent,
monitor and respond to zoonoses, i.e. diseases which can be spread to humans from animals,
and to be better prepared for future zoonotic health threats. In view of this, DG SANTE is
working on a One Health Plan for zoonotic influenza.
(3) https://health.ec.europa.eu/publications/eu-global-health-strategy-better-health-all-
changing-world_en
8

Key work strands in 2026 will include preparatory work for the report to the Council on the
implementation of the 2023 Council Recommendation on stepping up EU actions to combat
antimicrobial resistance in a One Health approach. Addressing the impacts of climate change on
health through a One Health approach will be essential considering emerging infectious
diseases as well as the increasing risk of vector-borne disease outbreaks due to climate
change. Work will continue to use the European Climate and Health Observatory as a
strategic platform in this area. In addition, work will focus on developing and coordinating
strategic action plans for initiatives that require a One Health approach, with particular
emphasis on zoonoses. The Commission will also adopt a decision on collecting information on
antimicrobial resistance in seafood, based on the European Food Safety Authority’s opinion.
General objective 3: Supporting people, and
strengthening our societies and our social
models
DG SANTE will focus on disease prevention by addressing the key determinants of health,
through a life course approach that addresses well-being at all ages. This will help to decrease
health inequalities and reduce the disease burden at both the level of the individual and the
population, alleviating pressure on overstretched health systems.
Specific objective 3.1: Improving people’s health by reducing
the burden of non-communicable diseases
Digital technologies, especially social media, are increasingly impacting the mental health of
young people in the EU. In 2026, DG SANTE will launch an EU-wide inquiry on the broader
impacts of social media and excessive screentime on the mental health and
wellbeing of young people in the EU, in line with the Mission Letter of Commissioner
Várhelyi. In addition, DG SANTE will also continue to implement the actions stemming from the
2023 Communication on a comprehensive approach on mental health.
Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and the main factor for ill-health
and disability in the EU. In 2026, DG SANTE will work with Commission services and Member
States to initiate the flagship actions set out in the Safe Hearts Plan (4). This plan aims to
support the development of and make available new and more personalised ways of prevention
and treatment for people in Europe. This will support public health, competitiveness and
innovation in digitalisation and the use of AI. DG SANTE will also prepare and launch a large-
scale communications campaign linked to the Safe Hearts Plan in 2026.
(4) https://health.ec.europa.eu/publications/communication-eu-cardiovascular-health-plan-safe-
hearts-plan_en
9

As part of its work on preventive health, DG
SANTE will in 2026 publish an evaluation
of the Tobacco Products Directive and
the Tobacco Advertising Directive. This
will include examining young people’s
access to new types of tobacco and nicotine
products. In 2026 DG SANTE will follow up
on the conclusions of the evaluation with a
proposal for a revision of the Directives.
In 2026, DG SANTE will continue to implement Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan (5). This will
include the full publication of the 5th Edition of the European Code against Cancer, which
aims to raise public awareness of factors that can increase the risk of cancer and of other non-
communicable diseases such as cardiovascular diseases that share common risk factors. The
EU Network of Comprehensive Cancer Centres will deliver training, guidelines and projects
to improve quality and access to cancer prevention, diagnostics and treatment. It will also
continue to work on the EU Comprehensive Cancer Centres certification.
General Objective 4: Sustaining our quality of
life: food security, water and nature
DG SANTE aims to ensure that the EU’s extensive legislation on food and feed safety and
animal and plant health is properly implemented, and to simplify it where possible. It
systematically adopts a “One Health” approach to preparedness and prevention, integrating
human, animal, plant and environmental health. These efforts have a positive impact on the
EU’s competitiveness. Directly, they promote innovation leading to new products for consumers,
farmers and businesses. Indirectly, they foster a more stable and predictable market
environment. DG SANTE works with non-EU countries and engage with relevant international
organisations to promote food safety, plant health, animal health and welfare standards
globally.
(5) https://commission.europa.eu/topics/public-health/european-health-union/cancer-plan-
europe_en
10

Specific objective 4.1: Contributing to the competitiveness of
the food sector and ensuring food and feed safety
Concluding the legislative process for the
food and feed simplification package
will be one of DG SANTE’s top priorities. The
proposal, adopted in December 2025, covers
many areas, including plant protection
products, biocidal products, feed additives,
hygiene requirements, the status of
fermentation products obtained with
genetically modified micro-organisms,
official controls of plants at the border, and the application of pesticides by drones. The
proposal aims to accelerate market access for biocontrol pesticides, simplify procedures and
reduce burdens for companies, farmers and Member States, in line with the Competitiveness
Compass. In parallel, DG SANTE will carry out non-legislative actions for faster access of
biopesticides to the market, for example targeted updates of guidance documents for
microorganisms, botanicals, viruses, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and metabolites, as well as
continued support for training and capacity building in Member States. An implementation
dialogue on feed will take place in the second half of the year.
DG SANTE works to address increasing concerns about the reduction of plant protection
solutions in farmers’ toolboxes to support Integrated Pest Management practices. In
this context, the DG expects an increased number of Decisions on the (renewal of) approval of
active substances, as EFSA will deliver conclusions for many substances where ‘stop the clock’
periods to assess endocrine disrupting properties are due to come to an end. In addition, data
requirements and uniform principles for assessing applications to authorise plant protection
products by Member States will be updated to ensure assessments are robust and fit-for-
purpose, and enable the possible endorsement and implementation of recently updated
guidance documents.
DG SANTE will continue to implement the Regulation on Maximum Residue Levels (MRLs) for
pesticides in food, including setting and reviewing MRLs for active substances and food
commodities as required.
DG SANTE will continue the evaluation of the Biocidal Products Regulation, including an
ongoing public consultation and a reality check. Numerous decisions on active substance
approvals from the ongoing review programme are also expected in this area, as well as
decisions on renewing approvals. Similarly, the number of decisions on Union Authorisations of
biocidal products is set to increase.
Preparatory work for an impact assessment to simplify the legislation on food contact
materials (FCM) for companies and authorities will continue, with ongoing consultations of
stakeholders and Member States. A reality check on the issue is also planned. In addition,
several plastic recycling processes will be authorised. The re-evaluation programme for food
additives will continue, as will preparations for establishing the Union list of food enzymes.
New novel foods will also be authorised. Additionally, maximum levels for contaminants
11

significant for food and feed safety will be established, such as mineral oils in food and furans
in baby food.
DG SANTE will work towards the 2030 legally binding food waste reduction targets in the
recently amended Waste Framework Directive. This includes starting work on related
implementing acts and studies, continuing the activities of the EU Platform on Food Losses and
Food Waste and providing grants for economic operators and Member States for initiatives to
reduce food waste and support food waste measurement, in cooperation with ESTAT.
DG SANTE will finalise the performance evaluation of EFSA, including the preparation of a
Commission Staff Working Document that will identify areas where EFSA could become more
efficient and better support applicants. DG SANTE will also start following up on the European
Court of Auditors’ report on food labelling. This will include preparing to adopt rules on the
voluntary provision of information on the possible and unintentional presence of allergens in
foods, the analysis of food labelling practices on the EU market, and regular exchanges with
stakeholders, including Member States, to improve how food labelling rules are applied.
Following the provisional political agreement between the European Parliament and Council on
rules applicable to plants produced by certain new genomic techniques (NGTs), the co-
legislators are expected to formally adopt the Regulation in the first half of 2026.
Implementation work (including preparation of the necessary delegated and implementing acts)
would then start in 2026 with a view to the application of the Regulation two years after entry
into force. This Regulation is vital to support the competitiveness of the European farming and
breeding sectors. DG SANTE will support the co-legislators during the interinstitutional
negotiations on the proposal on the production and marketing of Plant Reproductive
Material.
The potential impact of plant pests and animal and food-borne diseases on the EU
territory remains a concern. DG SANTE will continue work resulting from the 2024 amendment
of the Plant Health Regulation and ensure the implementation of the Animal Health Law,
the Official Controls Regulation and the EU legislation on veterinary medicinal
products. Every opportunity will be taken to streamline the comprehensive legal framework for
animal and plant health, animal welfare, feed, food hygiene and official controls and to ensure
more efficient implementation in a fully harmonised way.
DG SANTE’s stress-testing activities include the evaluation of the Animal Health Law, after a
study was completed in 2025. As part of the continuous management of that legislation, DG
SANTE has planned new delegated acts for the non-commercial movement of pets and to
revise the implementing rules for animal by-products. A possible revision of the rules for
transmissible spongiform encephalopathies (TSE) will also be considered, in addition to the
changes planned in the simplification package. DG SANTE will lead a discussion with the
Member States on the possible use of innovative tools in meat inspection.
In line with the Vision for Agriculture and Food, DG SANTE will increase efforts aimed at
checking that non-EU countries respect the EU’s sanitary and phytosanitary
requirements and help candidate countries prepare for joining the EU. At the same time,
Commission controls in Member States, which support the consistent and coherent application
12

of EU rules across the Single Market, will continue to make up a significant part of DG SANTE’s
work.
The Health and Food Audits and Analysis work programme for 2026 includes 158 planned
Commission controls – complemented by “on-demand” controls and other activities – around
food and feed safety, animal health, animal welfare, plant health and certain areas of human
health protection. The focus, and the corresponding percentage of controls, on non-EU countries
will be higher than in previous years.
In line with the Vision for Agriculture and Food, DG SANTE will take a leading role in a dedicated
Task Force for strengthening the controls on imports.
In 2026, DG SANTE will promote a One
Health approach and promote and defend
EU standards in international bodies.
These include the World Trade Organisation
(WTO), International Standard Setting Bodies
(Codex Alimentarius, the World Organisation
for Animal Health (WOAH), the International
Plant Protection Convention (IPPC), UN
agencies, the Organisation for Economic Co-
operation and Development (OECD) and the International Union for the Protection of New
Varieties of Plants (UPOV). DG SANTE will actively participate and contribute to activities under
the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Cartagena Protocol (CP) on Biosafety. DG
SANTE will continue to pursue positive bilateral relations on health and food safety with key
commercial partners, including the UK, Switzerland, Türkiye, the US, China, India, and Mercosur
countries. It will continue monitoring the implementation of the Windsor Framework (6).
Coordinating candidate countries’ preparedness for enlargement in the areas of health and
food safety will become an even bigger task than in the past.
DG SANTE will continue to manage the Better Training for Safer Food (BTSF) initiative. This
improves the knowledge and harmonised implementation of EU rules on food and feed law,
animal health and welfare, as well as One Health (e.g. antimicrobial resistance), plant health
and plant protection products in Member States, candidate countries and non-EU countries.
(6) The Windsor Framework is how the Protocol on Ireland / Northern Ireland is referred to in
accordance with Joint Declaration No 1/2023 of the Union and the United Kingdom in the
Joint Committee established by the Agreement on the withdrawal of the United Kingdom of
Great Britain and Northern Ireland from the European Union and the European Atomic Energy
Community of 24 March 2023 (OJ L 102, 17.4.2023, p. 87).
13

Specific objective 4.2: Modernising animal welfare based on
latest scientific evidence and strengthening the single
market
DG SANTE will lead the preparations for a legislative proposal on on-farm welfare planned
for adoption in the last quarter of the year. The overall goal is to modernise existing EU
Directives for on-farm animal welfare and to ensure a uniform and high level of protection of
animal welfare, fair competition for farmers, reduced administrative burden, better
enforcement and that ethical expectations are met. Preparations include an external impact
assessment study and consultations with the EU Animal Welfare Platform, building on a public
consultation already concluded in 2025. The proposal will constitute a follow-up, for certain
species and categories of animals, to the European Citizens’ initiative ‘End the cage age’ (7). DG
SANTE will also lead on the follow-up to the European Citizens’ Initiative “Fur Free
Europe” that will be announced in a Commission Communication in the first quarter of the
year.
DG SANTE will continue to support the co-legislators’ negotiations on the legislative proposal on
animal transport. In parallel, we are preparing for implementation after negotiations
conclude, with studies focusing on provisions on digitalisation to be finalised in 2026. Following
the provisional agreement on the new Regulation on the welfare of dogs and cats and
traceability, DG SANTE will work on an implementation strategy and start the first step of this
work, including sending a mandate to EFSA and starting to work on tertiary legislation set out in
the new legislation.
DG SANTE cooperates closely with Member States and stakeholder organisations. The work of
the Platform on Animal Welfare ensures a wide spectrum of stakeholder involvement and is an
essential tool to foster dialogue and avoid polarisation. The Animal Welfare expert group
provides a forum for discussion between DG SANTE and Member State authorities focusing on
implementation.
More information on outputs planned for 2026 is available in Annex 1.
(7) https://food.ec.europa.eu/animals/animal-welfare/eci/eci-end-cage-age_en
14

PART 3. A modern and sustainable public
administration: outputs in 2026
The internal control framework supports sound management and decision-making. In particular,
it ensures that risks to the achievement of objectives are addressed and reduced to acceptable
levels through cost-effective controls.
DG SANTE has established an internal control system tailored to its particular characteristics
and circumstances. The effective functioning of this internal control system will be assessed on
an ongoing basis throughout the year and will be subject to an annual assessment covering all
internal control principles.
A. Human resource management
In 2026, the results of the 2025 staff survey will be analysed and used to develop action that
can address potential concerns and weaknesses.
DG SANTE will pay extra attention to increasing cohesion and collaboration between the
different health policy strands, including between the different geographical sites, by continuing
to promote the ‘one health’ vision. Activities such as speed networking, happy hours, team
building and senior management talks will be intensified. Despite the growing discrepancy
between limited human resources and the ever-increasing need for action by the Commission
in the health and food domains, this work will help ensure that DG SANTE’s staff engagement
index stays above the Commission average. It provides a boost for staff to help them go the
extra mile and deliver under very stressful conditions.
DG SANTE will also strive to maintain its achievement at the beginning of this Commission
mandate on gender balance among managers (56% of middle managers were female). To
maintain this level of representation, the intention is to recruit at least 2 new female Heads of
Unit and 2 new female Deputy Heads of Unit. DG SANTE remains committed to support, on the
one hand, staff with disabilities by designing specific tailor-made adjustments with the support
services, and, on the other hand, to draw on the expertise of the Diversity and Inclusion Office
for all other specific needs that may arise.
Please refer to the performance tables in Annex 2 for more details on the outputs.
B. Digital transformation and data management
DG SANTE will advance its digital transformation, guided by its annual data and digital
master plan (aligning both local data and digital strategies and implementation actions), as
well as its multi-annual modernisation and rationalisation plan. DG SANTE aims to embed a
digital-first mindset across all its work.
15

DG SANTE will improve its digital culture via upskilling and a collaborative environment. This
will include knowledge hours and training sessions on AI and modern work methods. Networks
of champions for AI, security and M365/Teams will continue to connect staff with in-house
experts, reinforced by dedicated programmes and sessions on security and AI, in line with the
2025 AI change management plan.
DG SANTE will improve its infrastructure for digital readiness. It will host knowledge sessions on
digital-ready policymaking and encourage to follow corporate training sessions in that
respect. Multidisciplinary teams (with expertise in policy, legal, data, semantic and technical
matters) will bring IT and policy divisions closer and ensure digital impact assessments.
On Data-driven digital transformation, DG SANTE will streamline workflows combining
automation, innovation and AI. It is rationalising manual processes by using robotic
automation with Power Automate, for example to improve payment processes and automate
invoicing.
Continuous delivery and improvements to flagship digital systems will remain vital for
interoperability, the accessibility of health data and transparent data flows. These flagships
include the ERN Clinical Patient Management System 2.0, MyHealth@EU and HealthData@EU.
Tools such as the Health Technology Assessment Platform and the European Database on
Medical Devices (Eudamed) within the Medical Device Regulations will digitalise and simplify
processes, reducing administrative burden. Important cloud upgrade work will also take place
on systems like TRACES, the Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed and Food Information Portal
for better scalability and business continuity. Collaborative tools for external stakeholders,
including the Food Losses and Waste Hub and Anti-Microbial Resistance One Health Network
Platform, will be improved.
For a seamless digital environment, DG SANTE will continue to rationalise its IT
portfolio to replace legacy systems using a reuse-before-buy, before-build (RBB) approach,
integrating cutting-edge technologies from within the reusable solutions portfolio (RSP), making
use of corporate solutions, integrating smaller systems within common systems and phasing
out systems while modernising the portfolio. Cloud migration and technological modernisation
remain essential. Reusable solutions, available in the corporate catalogue, will be used, such as
eDelivery, and DG SANTE will continue to collaborate and contribute to corporate solutions such
as the European Crisis Management Platform (ECMP) and CASE@EC. Our cloud adoption efforts
align with the corporate strategy, Cloud Council recommendations and by ensuring all new
developments default to cloud capabilities while following all corporate actions and guidance
on European Commission Security and Resilience standards.
DG SANTE will continue to promote the ‘Digital Workplace Portal’, where staff can find
useful IT resources. On cybersecurity, adhering to the EC Cybersecurity strategy for 2025-2026,
DG SANTE will hold regular knowledge hours and maintain inventories in corporate governance
catalogues, with annual security control attestations to ensure adherence to security standards.
Comprehensive security plans and implementing panic buttons for enhanced protection will be
further developed and risk maturity improved. Dashboards will be used to track progress.
Greening initiatives involve reducing data storage needs through robotic process automation,
improved workflows and awareness through Eco-Management and Audit Scheme (EMAS)
sessions. Creating a more detailed EMAS page on the DG SANTE SharePoint will strengthen
16

communication efforts, reinforcing a commitment to sustainable infrastructure. Efforts to
phase out unit drives in favour of modern solutions like Teams and SharePoint will continue.
DG SANTE will continue to implement its Data Strategy, building on its foundation of
designated data owners and stewards for its data assets to increase data maturity. DG SANTE
will continue to contribute new data assets to the EC Data Catalogue. These assets may
originate from its IT solutions, acquisitions, or other sources. DG SANTE will streamline and
harmonise procedures for data acquisition, reinforcing its commitment to effective data
management practices. DG SANTE will improve the use of its Data Platform to ensure that
the FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable) principles apply to all data assets.
The Platform provides machine-to-machine interfaces, streamlining cross-solution capabilities
and promoting interoperability. Adopting common data standards, including developing a new
European Health Record Exchange Format, will harmonise how health data is shared across
systems, enabling more efficient primary care delivery and unlocking the full potential of
secondary data use for innovation and research.
DG SANTE will offer targeted internal training sessions and encourage participation in
relevant corporate training programmes on data. DG SANTE will continue to uphold strict
compliance with personal data rules and integrate robust practices at all levels, emphasising
the principles of personal data protection by design and by default. It will maintain updated and
regularly reviewed records of processing activities. A comprehensive review of all data
processing operations is conducted biennially. Raising awareness among staff remains a
priority, with obligatory training for new employees, and general and specialised training for all
staff.
C. Sound financial management
DG SANTE’s latest internal controls strategy was adopted by the Management Board in January
2025. It takes account of changes in the DG’s control structure following the transfer of budget
implementation tasks to HaDEA, the recast of the Financial Regulation and the roll-out of
SUMMA. It includes control and anti-fraud measures for all types of expenditure directly
managed by the DG. It has risk assessment and risk management integrated into the planning
process, and control activities including ex-ante desk and on-the-spot verifications.
DG SANTE will continue to ensure that the estimated risk at payment for its cost-based
expenditure stays below 2% of relevant expenditure. It will strive to have cost-effective
controls in place to guarantee the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions and
ensure that regulatory provisions and accounting closure instructions are complied with. It will
regularly monitor indicators to assess budget execution and timeliness of payments (see
performance tables in Annex 3 for details of the DG’s outputs and indicators). DG SANTE will
implement and monitor the action plans for audits set out by the Commission's Internal Audit
Service and the European Court of Auditors.
Under the lead of DG BUDG, HR and SG, DG SANTE will contribute to the cost-benefit analysis
(CBA) for the direct programme implementation 2028-2034.
17

D. Fraud risk management
DG SANTE has developed and implemented its own anti-fraud strategy and action plan since
2013, based on a fraud risk assessment and methodology provided by OLAF. The controls to
prevent and detect fraud are the same as those intended to ensure the legality and regularity
of transactions. An assessment of fraud risks is included in the annual risk management
exercise. In 2026, DG SANTE will continue to strengthen its cooperation with OLAF and EPPO.
DG SANTE aims to help put the revised Commission Anti-Fraud Strategy’s Action plan (8) into
action and take part in OLAF’s awareness-raising activities on anti-fraud matters through the
network on Fraud Prevention and Detection. Relevant feedback will be provided to DG SANTE’s
financial cell.
In 2026, DG SANTE will finalise the process of updating its anti-fraud strategy and preparing its
action plan for 2026-2028 that reflects the Commission’s Anti-Fraud Strategy and its latest
action plan. In addition, DG SANTE will continue to raise awareness among its staff through
ethics and anti-fraud training courses and by promoting relevant guidelines. Performance
tables in Annex 3 show details of DG SANTE’s outputs and indicators on fraud risk
management.
E. Sound environmental management
To fulfil the Commission's commitment to become carbon neutral by 2030, its greenhouse gas
emissions have to be reduced by at least 38% compared to 2019. This requires a significant
reduction in the environmental impact of missions, meetings and conferences (the baseline in
2019 for DG SANTE is 2 110 (9) tonnes of CO emissions for staff professional travel). Within
